questions.def: Use present perfect to describe a state that started in the past.
questions.question: I ___ him since we were children.

questions.def: Use past simple for completed actions in the past.
questions.question: She ___ to the party last night.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had eaten' shows action completed before another past action.
questions.question: We ___ dinner before you arrived.

questions.def: Past continuous describes an action in progress at a specific time.
questions.question: They ___ TV when I called.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had' shows a completed action before another action.
questions.question: By the time he arrived, she ___ already left.

questions.def: 'have known' is the correct present perfect tense.
questions.question: I am knowing him since last year.

questions.def: Use past simple 'lived' because the action is finished.
questions.question: She ___ in London for ten years and then moved.

questions.def: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + infinitive.
questions.question: If I ___ more money, I would buy a car.

questions.def: Reported speech: 'will' changes to 'would'.
questions.question: He said he ___ come to the party.

questions.def: 'has been working' is correct with 'since'.
questions.question: She is working here since May.

questions.def: 'am going to' expresses future plans or intentions.
questions.question: I ___ going to call you later.

questions.def: Use present continuous 'am going' for planned future actions.
questions.question: I ___ to the cinema tomorrow.

questions.def: Use present simple 'play' for habitual actions.
questions.question: They ___ football every Sunday.

questions.def: Past simple 'worked' for a completed action in the past.
questions.question: He ___ all day yesterday.

questions.def: Present perfect 'has been' for a state that started in the past.
questions.question: She ___ happy since she got the job.

questions.def: Past continuous 'were doing' for actions in progress.
questions.question: What ___ you doing when I called?

questions.def: 'have lived' or 'have been living' is needed with 'for'.
questions.question: I am living here for three years.

questions.def: Past simple 'saw' for a completed action in the past.
questions.question: I ___ him yesterday.

questions.def: Future perfect shows completion before a future time.
questions.question: By next year, I ___ here for five years.

questions.def: Past perfect for an action completed before another past action.
questions.question: He ___ English before he moved to London.

questions.def: 'has already finished' is the correct present perfect tense.
questions.question: She is already finished her homework.

questions.def: Past simple 'went' for a completed action in the past.
questions.question: They ___ to Italy last summer.

questions.def: 'will' expresses a future intention or prediction.
questions.question: He ___ be here in five minutes.

questions.def: Second conditional: If + past simple (were), would + infinitive.
questions.question: If I ___ you, I would study harder.

questions.def: Past continuous describes action in progress at a past time.
questions.question: It ___ when I left the house.

questions.def: Reported speech: present simple 'is' changes to past simple 'was'.
questions.question: She told me she ___ tired.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had' shows completion before another action.
questions.question: They ___ already eaten when we arrived.

questions.def: Past simple tense because the party was last night.
questions.question: She ___ to the party last night because she was sick.

questions.def: Past simple for an action that happened during another past action.
questions.question: I ___ my keys while I was running in the park.

questions.def: Should be 'has been living' for actions started in the past and continuing now.
questions.question: He is living in London since 2010.
